scope.note: A national planning level is not a forecast for any one county, city, or utility.

headline: Top Off the Pantry
summary: Elevated background risk. Keep about two weeks of food and water. No panic buying.
supplyWindow: About 2 weeks of food and water
rationale: Level 4 holds. The newest confirmed national fuel stock data are still EIA's Weekly Petroleum Status Report for the week ending October 30, 2026: distillate stocks of 99.3 million barrels, 11.0 percent below a year earlier, and Strategic Petroleum Reserve crude of 282.2 million barrels. The delayed report for the following week is scheduled for release at noon and 2:00 p.m. eastern time today, November 12, after this review. AAA's national average diesel price on November 12 was $6.10 a gallon, down from $6.26 a week earlier but far above $3.76 a year ago, and regular gasoline fell below $3.91, so fuel stays expensive and tight rather than unavailable. Brent crude traded near $92 on November 12, near a two-month low, as Gulf output rose. Overseas risk did not ease in substance. Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy said two supertankers were disabled by explosions overnight while using what it called an unauthorized route through the Strait of Hormuz, after at least three other tanker strikes or possible strikes on November 10 and 11. Iran's security chief threatened on November 11 to strike U.S. bases as far away as Europe if the United States attacks Iran again, and the Treasury Secretary was moved to a military base after Iranian threats; these are threats and protective moves, not new attacks on the United States. Taiwan's defense ministry reported a Chinese joint combat readiness patrol of 29 aircraft on November 12, the second this month, with no blockade or attack reported. U.S. envoys met Russia's president in Moscow on November 12 after the Abu Dhabi talks ended with a prisoner-swap deal but no ceasefire. No confirmed disruption of fuel, power, food distribution, or payments across multiple U.S. regions was found. Rolling outages for about 61,000 customers in Puerto Rico, Sierra Nevada winter storm warnings, and Alaska blizzard and marine warnings are regional and are not averaged into the national number, and the National Hurricane Center expects no tropical cyclone formation in the next 7 days. Level 3 would need a confirmed multi-region disruption; none was confirmed today.
disclaimer: PANTRYCON is an independent, unofficial household preparedness assessment for the United States. It is not affiliated with the U.S. government or the armed forces. It is not DEFCON, and it is not a civil-defense or military alert. The number is a national planning snapshot. It does not mean every community faces the same immediate threat.
overrides: Follow local official instructions first. Evacuation orders, boil-water notices, shelter-in-place orders, and other location-specific emergency alerts always override this national level.

evidence.title: U.S. distillate fuel oil stocks
evidence.summary: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report Table 6 lists distillate fuel oil stocks at 99.3 million barrels for the week ending October 30, 2026, compared with 102.8 million the prior week (difference shown as -3.6) and 111.5 million a year earlier (percent change shown as -11.0).
evidence.limits: This is a national stock figure for diesel and heating oil at refineries, in pipelines, and at bulk terminals. It is not a count of fuel at neighborhood stations, and it is not an outage report. East Coast (PADD 1) distillate stocks were 22.6 million barrels, up from 21.8 the prior week. Gulf Coast (PADD 3) stocks were 40.5 million, down from 43.4.

source.label: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report, Table 6

evidence.title: Strategic Petroleum Reserve crude
evidence.summary: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report Table 1 lists Strategic Petroleum Reserve crude at 282.2 million barrels for the week ending October 30, 2026, compared with 282.6 million the prior week. The year-earlier figure on that table is 409.6 million barrels.
evidence.limits: A smaller strategic crude stock is context for the national fuel buffer. It is not, by itself, a household supply emergency, and this page does not turn it into a price forecast.

source.label: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report, Table 1

evidence.title: National average retail diesel price
evidence.summary: AAA's national average table, priced as of November 12, 2026, lists diesel at $6.0977 a gallon, compared with $6.1306 the day before, $6.2564 a week earlier, $6.2665 a month earlier, and $3.7568 a year earlier. Regular gasoline is listed at $3.9081, down from $4.1003 a week earlier.
evidence.limits: A retail price average shows cost pressure, not whether fuel is physically available at stations.

evidence.title: No newer weekly petroleum report yet
evidence.summary: The inventory figures above stop at the week ending October 30, 2026. EIA's schedule says the delayed Weekly Petroleum Status Report will be released on Thursday, November 12, 2026, at 12:00 p.m. and 2:00 p.m. eastern time, because the federal government was closed on Wednesday, November 11.
evidence.limits: Whether stocks kept falling after October 30 is not known in this snapshot. This review was completed before the scheduled release time, so the new figures are not reflected here.

source.label: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report schedule

evidence.title: Crude oil near a two-month low
evidence.summary: CNBC, citing Reuters, reported that Brent crude futures were down 37 cents at $92.39 a barrel and U.S. West Texas Intermediate was at $86.16 at 0946 GMT on November 12, 2026, after both fell more than $1 in early Asian trading, and that both were headed for a weekly fall. The report said OPEC+ crude production rose in October, led by higher Saudi output, despite shipping disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz.
evidence.limits: A futures price is a market reading, not a measure of fuel on hand in the United States, and this page does not turn it into a forecast.

evidence.title: Nationwide grid emergency
evidence.summary: This review did not confirm an active nationwide electricity emergency from a grid operator or a federal energy office, and did not find a new multi-region outage reported on November 11 or 12, 2026. El Nuevo Dia reported on November 11 that rolling outages left more than 61,000 customers without power in Puerto Rico, and a local outage affected about 7,000 customers in one Utah community. These are regional events. The level is not based on a live outage map.
evidence.limits: A gap in this snapshot is not an all-clear. Local outages can be serious while the national planning level stays at 4.

evidence.title: Nationwide cyber disruption
evidence.summary: This review did not confirm a nationwide cyber disruption of U.S. utilities, pipelines, grocery cold chains, or payment systems on November 11 or 12, 2026. Cyber items seen were agency warnings and planning announcements, not new U.S. incidents. Social-media claims were not used.
evidence.limits: A later confirmation from an operator or from CISA could raise the level. Absence from this page is not a finding that nothing happened.

evidence.title: France blames Iranian cyber unit for supermarket fridge sabotage
evidence.summary: NPR reported on November 9, 2026 that France's national cybersecurity agency said Iranian military hackers took over refrigeration controllers at about 700 retail sites in France in October, raising temperatures overnight and spoiling food, and also hit several small hydroelectric plants with moderate effects. France linked the Shahid Kaveh unit to Iran's Revolutionary Guard, and Paris prosecutors are seeking international arrest warrants. Grocery stores in other European countries were hit in similar attacks the week before.
evidence.limits: This is an attack in Europe. NPR notes that refrigeration failures at U.S. military commissaries in August have not been officially attributed or confirmed as cyberattacks, and this review found no confirmed attack on U.S. grocery supply.

evidence.title: Federal warning on refrigeration and cold-chain controllers
evidence.summary: On November 5, 2026, CISA, the FBI, HHS, USDA, and the Department of Transportation published a fact sheet warning of ongoing cyber threat activity against industrial refrigeration and cold-chain monitoring systems. CISA said actors worldwide are targeting unpatched or internet-exposed temperature and refrigeration controllers in retail grocery and cold storage, which could change temperatures and cause loss of inventory, and urged operators to take those devices off the internet and patch them.
evidence.limits: This is a warning and guidance, not a report of a U.S. outage or of spoiled U.S. food supplies.

evidence.title: Sierra winter storm warnings, Alaska blizzard and marine warnings, and Pacific coast surf
evidence.summary: This snapshot is not connected to a live National Weather Service or FEMA feed. A check of active NWS alerts early on November 12, 2026 listed winter storm warnings for the Sierra Nevada in California and Nevada, including the Lake Tahoe area, Mono County, the eastern Sierra slopes of Inyo County, and Lassen Volcanic National Park; high surf warnings on the northern California coast; blizzard warnings on Alaska's Arctic coast; gale and heavy freezing spray warnings off Alaska and the Pacific coast; and a flood watch for Mason County, Washington. The flood warnings in Florida, Texas, and Arizona listed a day earlier were no longer among active warnings. These are regional events and are not averaged into the national number. The U.S. Geological Survey's list of significant earthquakes for the past week showed no U.S. earthquake.
evidence.limits: A local warning can require action immediately, including when the national level is 4 or 5.

evidence.title: No tropical cyclones
evidence.summary: The National Hurricane Center's Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook issued at 7:00 AM EST on November 12, 2026 says tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days for the North Atlantic, Caribbean Sea, and Gulf.
evidence.limits: This covers tropical storms only. It says nothing about winter storms, floods, or earthquakes.

source.label: NHC Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook, Nov 12, 2026

evidence.title: Nationwide civil disruption
evidence.summary: This review did not confirm a nationwide civil disruption that is stopping household resupply, and found no invocation of the Insurrection Act as of November 12, 2026. Coverage seen discussed earlier refusals to rule it out around the midterm elections; it did not report an invocation. Prediction-market prices were not used.
evidence.limits: A local emergency order still overrides this page.

evidence.title: Attack on Saudi East-West pipeline
evidence.summary: Saudi Arabia's energy ministry said on November 9, 2026 that the East-West pipeline was targeted in the Madinah region, causing a limited fire that emergency teams put out, with no injuries and pipeline operations unaffected. The pipeline is Saudi Arabia's main route for moving crude to the Red Sea without passing through the Strait of Hormuz.
evidence.limits: The ministry did not name the attacker. This review found no confirmed effect on U.S. fuel supplies.

source.label: Arab News, citing the Saudi energy ministry, Nov 9, 2026

evidence.title: Houthi missile attack damages Aramco tower in Riyadh
evidence.summary: Reuters reported on November 8, 2026 that windows were blown out across several floors of Aramco's corporate tower in Riyadh's financial district. Saudi Arabia's energy ministry said the damage came from debris of an attempted attack, was limited, and caused no injuries. The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted Houthi missiles fired at Riyadh and the Eastern Province.
evidence.limits: Houthi claims that they also hit Aramco storage tanks, the Abqaiq facility, and Riyadh's airport were not confirmed by Saudi authorities. This is an attack on Saudi territory, not on the United States, and this review found no confirmed effect on U.S. fuel supplies.

evidence.title: More tanker attacks in and near the Strait of Hormuz
evidence.summary: Reuters, in the Oman Observer, reported on November 12, 2026 that Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy said two oil supertankers were disabled by large explosions on the night of November 11 after ignoring warnings against using an unauthorized route in the strait, and Iranian state media said they hit naval mines. Seatrade Maritime reported the same day that the supertanker Fujairah Energy was hit by a projectile on November 10, injuring four of its 22 crew, that the tanker Sea 1 was struck by a drone on November 10 with all crew safe, and that the tanker NCC Fajr was involved in a possible attack on November 11. The head of the International Maritime Organization repeated his call for shipowners not to send crews through the strait.
evidence.limits: The Revolutionary Guards' account and the mine claims were not independently confirmed, and the ships were not named in the Reuters report. In several earlier cases UKMTO said tankers were struck by unknown projectiles. This review found no confirmed disruption of fuel imports reaching U.S. households.

evidence.title: U.S. blockade enforcement in the Gulf of Oman
evidence.summary: U.S. Central Command said that on November 7, 2026 a U.S. military aircraft fired on the stern of the St. Kitts-flagged cargo ship Huda and disabled it in the Gulf of Oman after the crew ignored repeated warnings and tried to break the naval blockade against Iran. CENTCOM said enforcement since July has redirected 147 commercial vessels and disabled five merchant ships.
evidence.limits: This is a military enforcement action at sea, not an attack on the United States, and it does not report a U.S. supply disruption.

evidence.title: Iran threatens U.S. bases as far away as Europe
evidence.summary: RTE reported on November 11, 2026 that Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei said in a televised interview that if U.S. aircraft take off from a base, even one in Europe or another distant region, to bomb Iran, Iran will strike those bases too. The report said Tehran still demands that Washington unfreeze assets and lift sanctions before the Strait of Hormuz reopens, and that the Secretary of State said on November 10 there was no need to attack Iran again. A day earlier, Al Jazeera and Reuters reported that Rezaei denied that talks with Washington were under way and said the strait will stay shut until Iran's conditions are met.
evidence.limits: These are statements about a possible renewed war, not a reported new attack. There is no agreed outcome, and both escalation and a deal remain possible. The statements did not change confirmed U.S. household supplies in this review.

evidence.title: U.S. aircraft moved from a British base over an Iranian threat
evidence.summary: Reuters, via Al Jazeera, reported on November 10, 2026 that, according to The Wall Street Journal, U.S. refueling tankers using RAF Mildenhall in England were diverted to Germany and other locations on November 9 after a threat from Iran, and that security at RAF Mildenhall and RAF Lakenheath was raised to Force Protection Condition Charlie.
evidence.limits: The nature of the threat was not made public. The UK defense ministry and the U.S. Air Force did not confirm the reason, saying aircraft move for operational reasons. A force-protection move is not an attack and does not report a U.S. supply disruption.

evidence.title: Treasury Secretary moved to a military base after Iranian threats
evidence.summary: CBS News reported on November 11, 2026 that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent relocated from his Washington-area home to a military base following Iranian threats against his life. A Treasury spokesperson said he will not be deterred and remains committed to the sanctions campaign and the naval blockade against Iran.
evidence.limits: The relocation was reported through people familiar with the matter, and the severity of the threats was not made public. A protective move is not an attack and does not report a U.S. supply disruption.

evidence.title: Chinese joint combat readiness patrol near Taiwan
evidence.summary: Taiwan's defense ministry said that from 9:38 a.m. Taiwan time on November 12, 2026 it detected 29 Chinese military aircraft and drones, 22 of which crossed the Taiwan Strait median line or its extension into Taiwan's northern, central, southwestern, and eastern airspace, operating with Chinese warships in what China called a joint combat readiness patrol. The ministry's daily report for the 24 hours ending 6 a.m. that day listed 7 aircraft sorties, 7 navy ships, and 2 official ships. Taiwanese press reports said this was the second such patrol this month, after one on November 4.
evidence.limits: No blockade or attack on Taiwan was reported. This review found no confirmed effect on U.S. household supplies.

source.label: Taiwan Ministry of National Defense press release, Nov 12, 2026

evidence.title: U.S. envoys meet Russia's president after Abu Dhabi talks
evidence.summary: The Associated Press reported that U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived at the Kremlin on November 12, 2026 for talks with Russia's president, after two days of U.S.-mediated Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi ended on November 11 with agreement on a large prisoner exchange. Reuters reported that no wider breakthrough was announced and that differences remain, including on territory, and that the envoys plan to meet Ukraine's president in Dublin later the same day.
evidence.limits: Fighting continues and no ceasefire has been agreed. No NATO-Russia clash was reported, and this review found no confirmed effect on U.S. household supplies.

evidence.title: State Department worldwide caution
evidence.summary: On November 6, 2026, the State Department's TravelGov account warned U.S. citizens abroad of increased threats from Iranian-supported groups, Iranian efforts to target U.S. officials, and possible flight cancellations or airspace closures.
evidence.limits: This is a travel advisory for Americans abroad. It is not an attack order, and it does not report a domestic supply disruption.

source.label: U.S. Department of State, TravelGov, Nov 6, 2026

raise: A later EIA or Energy Department report of a physical fuel-distribution failure across more than one region, rather than lower stocks alone.
A verified multi-state electricity emergency long enough to interrupt ordinary food resupply.
A confirmed cyber disruption of pipelines, payment systems, or grid operations with household effects, stated by the operator or by CISA.
Official emergency declarations that restrict movement or commerce across many states at the same time.
Concurrent verified disasters that break national distribution, as distinct from a single local storm.
lower: A later Weekly Petroleum Status Report showing distillate stocks rebuilding toward the prior-year level, without a physical distribution failure.
No verified multi-region outage of power, fuel, food, or payments in the sources reviewed that week.
A return to level 5 when the several-day Ready.gov basic kit is again the matching band, because background fuel tightness is no longer the best reading.

levels.name: Normal Larder
levels.means: Routine conditions. Keep the Ready.gov basic kit: several days of food and water, at about one gallon of water per person per day.
levels.doesNotMean: It does not mean a particular town is free of storms, outages, or local alerts.

levels.name: Top Off the Pantry
levels.means: Elevated background risk without a verified nationwide emergency. Keep about two weeks of food and water at home, which matches the American Red Cross home-kit suggestion.
levels.doesNotMean: It does not mean a shortage is underway, and it is not a call to panic-buy.

levels.name: Deep Pantry
levels.means: A credible near-term disruption of grid, fuel, food distribution, or civil order affecting resupply across multiple regions, confirmed from a primary source.
levels.doesNotMean: A headline, a market move, or a single local storm is not enough to set this band.

levels.name: Bunkered
levels.means: An imminent or unfolding disruption of food, fuel, power, or payments across a large part of the country.
levels.doesNotMean: It is not a military mobilization order, and it is not a prediction.

levels.name: Full FORTRESS
levels.means: An active nationwide grid-down, or a supply-chain emergency that stops ordinary resupply for most U.S. households. The name is this project's label for that band.
levels.doesNotMean: It is not a military status, a DEFCON level, or a government order. This project does not use an official 90-day threshold from any agency.

checklist.intro: Practical targets for the current band. The basic items come from Ready.gov, the American Red Cross, and CDC water guidance. Buy and rotate what the household will actually use. This is not an order to empty a store.

groups.title: Food
items: About 14 days of foods the household already eats, leaning on items that need no refrigeration and little water to prepare.
A manual can opener.
Foods for infants, special diets, and medical nutrition if someone in the household needs them.
Ready.gov's basic kit is a several-day supply. This level uses the longer Red Cross home window of about two weeks.

groups.title: Water
items: About one gallon per person per day for drinking and sanitation. At this level that is about 14 gallons per person.
More if the climate is hot, someone is ill, or a medical need requires it. Ready.gov notes that needs vary.
Commercially sealed bottles, or food-grade containers kept as Ready.gov describes.
If tap water is unsafe, use bottled water or follow the local health department. CDC explains boiling and other treatment; do not drink water from radiators or boilers.

groups.title: Prescriptions and health
items: The Red Cross basic kit lists a 7-day supply of medications and medical items. This level does not stretch that into a 14-day rule.
Ask a doctor or pharmacist before setting aside an emergency supply of prescription medicine. Ready.gov gives the same caution.
A written list of medicines, doses, and allergies, plus glasses and hearing-aid batteries.
A small first-aid kit.

groups.title: Power banks and light
items: A charged phone, its charger, and a backup battery or power bank. Ready.gov includes a backup battery in the basic kit.
A flashlight and spare batteries.
This level does not ask households to buy a generator.

groups.title: Modest cash
items: Small bills.
Enough cash for food, fuel, and a few nights of lodging if card payments do not work. That is the Ready.gov citizen-preparedness guide's framing. This page does not set a dollar amount.

groups.title: Communications
items: A battery-powered or hand-crank radio. A NOAA Weather Radio is useful if you can get one.
A written list of out-of-area contacts, kept with the kit and not only in a phone.
Sign up for the local alert system where you live. This national page cannot do that for you.

groups.title: Accessibility, children, and pets
items: Daily assistive items: extra glasses, hearing-aid batteries, and a plan for devices that need power. Ready.gov's disability guidance says to talk with a clinician about equipment that must stay on.
Infant formula, bottles, and diapers if needed.

Pets: food, water, medicine, a carrier or leash, and ID. Ready.gov says public shelters often refuse pets, so know a place that will take them. If local officials say to evacuate, the pet should go too.
A support network and a paper contact list for anyone who would need help leaving.

methodology: A person reviews this snapshot on a 5-to-1 household scale. Five is the calm end and one is the critical end. The bands match the durations used by the companion household board: several days, about two weeks, about 30 days, about 60 days, and 90 days or more. Those durations are this project's planning labels. They are not agency thresholds. Categories reviewed each time are national energy and grid conditions, supply chains, cyber disruption, weather and disasters, civil disruption, and geopolitical risks that would change U.S. household supplies. Confirmed means the cited page states the fact. Developing means the picture is incomplete, such as a scheduled data gap. Unverified means this review did not confirm it, which is not proof that it is false. Prediction markets and social-media posts are not evidence. The page is a saved assessment with a review time. It is not a live feed, and it does not show a live indicator.
limitations: There is no live feed behind this page. The review time is the time a person last checked the sources.

The petroleum figures are for the week ending October 30, 2026. EIA's delayed Weekly Petroleum Status Report is scheduled for 12:00 p.m. and 2:00 p.m. eastern time on Thursday, November 12, 2026, after this review.
This review did not ingest a live weather, outage, or emergency-declaration map. Local alerts are outside the national number on purpose.
Unverified rows are gaps in the review. They are not findings that a category is calm.
No likelihood percentages, incident timelines, or official trigger values were added where a source did not state them.
Regional stock changes inside the EIA tables already show that a national total can hide opposite local moves.
